author.role: independent evaluator and confirmation case author

history.resolution: Both contested labels fixed in place: pfc4 g2-by-bike now charges the $1 unlock on any bike, and pfc2 g2-restructured now gives manual closing to the operators. Each oracle keeps a failing example of the same mistake (pfc4 b7-unlock-classic-only, pfc2 b7-crew-closes-by-hand). The automated prose screen the review found weak was removed rather than repaired: ticket 115 does not ask for one and lists a sole semantic-judge gate as out of scope. Grading now checks protected spans byte for byte and sends every prose output to adjudication against the oracle fact lists. Tests build their own review state, and contested_groups must name real group ids.

review.notes: Contested on contract labels. pfc2-adjacent-config: valid example g2-restructured (oracles/pfc2-adjacent-config.json:299) says 'The night crew can also close it manually'; the source gives manual closing to operators, so the actor change is not entailed. pfc4-conditional-quantity: valid example g2-by-bike (oracles/pfc4-conditional-quantity.json:370) puts the casual $1 unlock fee under 'On classic bikes' and leaves e-bikes at 15 cents a minute for all riders, so a casual e-bike rider reads no unlock fee; the source says $1 to unlock any bike. Each fix is a one-clause edit to that example, then --refreeze and a fresh second review. The other four groups' contracts and labeled outputs follow from their sources and requests. Screen findings (advisory, not grounds for replacing a group): new reviewer-written outputs drew false screen_fail verdicts on faithful text in all six groups (pfc1:82 'to get'; pfc2:233 'neither closes'; pfc3:28 'just three of'; pfc3:31 'aren't the only checks'; pfc4:250 'No one rides an e-bike free'; pfc4:251 'and e-bike' after a semicolon; pfc5:116 'can't promise we'll reopen Saturday'; pfc5:141 'Not all pools are closed'; pfc6:320 'isn't compressed right away'; pfc6:335 'nothing reports an error') and screen_pass on 21 of 25 clean unfaithful outputs. In pfc6, quoting the directive names satisfies every preserve check except missingok, so an explanation with every line wrong only reaches needs_adjudication. Reviewers must read every output; screen_pass is not evidence of fidelity. Freeze recomputed independently with hashlib and matches; edits to an input, a request, an oracle, the exposure record or the schedule each break the lock. No 8 or 6 word run is shared with a wider corpus (all of evals/ outside this set, skills/dispel, docs/, CHANGELOG.md).

second_review.notes: Approved for this freeze. An earlier pass on freeze e983e1d7 asked for changes and was never recorded here: failing examples listed fewer failures than the oracle's own questions gave them, and three questions overlapped. Those questions are now gone (pfc4 no-other-rates, pfc5 no-vague-cause, pfc6 directive-explained, with pfc6 b8). Each failing example now names one `shows` question and is not claimed to be complete. I read every input and checked each label myself. Each `shows` is a question its example really fails, and every valid example meets its contract and every remaining question. Example texts, contracts and fact lists are byte-identical to the previous freeze apart from the deleted b8. Borderline cases for the adjudicator: pfc5 g3 'due Thursday' under part-hedged, and pfc6 g3 'under /var/log/kiosk/' under path-scope (the glob does not recurse). No automated prose judgement remains. Grading checks protected spans byte for byte through protected_span_checks. --grade exits 1 on a lost span: a changed value, a tab indent and a dropped space each failed, and the intact bytes passed. I recomputed the freeze independently with hashlib and every input, request, span offset, oracle, cases.json and exposures digest matches.
